profile.campus: Helsinki, Finland (Equinix HE3, part of Equinix's Helsinki-region cluster)
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's HE3 facility at Parrukatu 2 in Helsinki, Finland, part of a cluster of Equinix buildings, HE3 through HE7, that the company markets collectively under its Helsinki region heading even though several sit in the neighboring cities of Vantaa and Espoo rather than Helsinki proper. Equinix's own dedicated page describes HE3 as a three-story, reinforced-concrete building with 1,220 square meters, about 13,132 square feet, of colocation space, N+1 power and cooling redundancy, generator autonomy of 30 hours or more at full load, and a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee, though it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about $3.8 billion, though Equinix's current HE3 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998 by former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers Al Avery and Jay Adelson, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX; the company's own about page states a current global footprint of 281 data centers across six continents, while Wikipedia separately cites approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries as of 2025.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Equinix HE3 in Helsinki is a 13,132-square-foot colocation facility with N+1 redundancy and 30-hour generator autonomy, but Equinix publishes no megawatt capacity figure for it.

The building sits in a five-facility cluster that Equinix markets as its Helsinki region even though some facilities occupy neighboring Vantaa and Espoo. This geographic bundling reflects how colocation operators structure their offerings around metropolitan areas and customer convenience rather than strict municipal boundaries. Equinix itself does not attribute HE3 to either of the two acquisitions that built its European footprint, IXEurope (2007) and TelecityGroup (2015), despite the latter representing the company's largest acquisition at $3.8 billion.

The data does not disclose HE3's actual power consumption or IT load capacity. Equinix's public facility page emphasizes redundancy, reliability guarantees, and backup duration but omits the megawatt figures that would let readers assess its role in regional compute infrastructure. As an EU facility, HE3 now falls under the Energy Efficiency Directive, which since 2024 requires data centers above a minimum threshold to report power usage effectiveness and water consumption to European Commission databases. This regulatory transparency exists in the EU but has no direct equivalent in most US markets, creating an asymmetry in what the public can know about comparable facilities.
